text.p: Italian debt markets ended with a buoyant tone as concerns that German interest rates might be tweaked higher shortly started to fade from the market.

Btps' attention focused on events abroad, with dollar moves keeping players on their toes and investors preferring to square positions as they awaited the outcome of the Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting today, although few expected a rate change.

One dealer noted interest in the cash Italian market for the first time in several days. The July 2007 Btp ended 38 basis points up at 101.55, with the yield at 6.63 percent and the spread against the 10-year Bund widening a shade to 106 bps.
The September futures contract on LIFFE was 58 basis points higher at 136.10 in late European trade, just below the session high of 136.14. Brokers cited resistance in the 136.30/40 area.
The lira had a fairly featureless day, scarcely budging from its opening levels and trading around 975.54/5.75 per mark and 1,795.00/7.00 per dollar.
There is little on the domestic front before preliminary August inflation data from 11 sample cities is released on August 21 and 22.
